settings.summary:
I found nine problems in the settings. Nothing was changed; I only read files. I did not launch the game. Something else started it twice while I was working: TS4_x64 at 23:52:52 and again at 00:01:11. A new 0-byte Mods\FitStudio\FitStudio.ts4script also appeared at 23:52:35.

1. **The PC is short of memory.** Config.log records free RAM when the game starts: 2,972 MB on 7/31 and only 306 MB on 9/23, out of 15,676 MB. Measured live, Windows had 693 MB free and 20.9 GB of the 60.7 GB C:\pagefile.sys in use (peak 42 GB). Committed memory was about 43.6 GB against a 76.4 GB limit. The biggest user was chrome.exe (PID 78604) with 11.7 GB private memory. Brave, Discord, several Claude processes and explorer (2.4 GB) added more. Constant use of the disk as overflow memory slows every load and causes stutter. This is the largest problem outside the mods themselves.
2. **An old graphics override file is active and switches off most culling and detail reduction.** The file is ConfigOverride\GraphicsRules.sgr, Simp4Sims "SGR Full 19-08-2021" (49,084 bytes). The "Edited by Simp4Sims" lines at the top of Config.log confirm it is loaded. Its changes against the stock E:\The Sims 4\Game\Bin\GraphicsRules.sgr:
   - Objects are almost never skipped for being small: ObjectSizeCullFactor is 9999 instead of 200.
   - Far draw distance (ClipPlaneDistances) is 9999 instead of 1000/1500 for High.
   - Objects always use their most detailed model: ObjectLODBias is 0.00 instead of 0.6666.
   - Sims always use their most detailed model: RenderSimLODDistances is 2999.97–3000 instead of 25/50/100/1000.
   - Sim textures are 2048 px at every distance instead of 2048/1024/512/128.
   - Shadow maps are 5120 px instead of 2048 (VeryHigh) and 3096 instead of 1024 (High).
   - Mirror and water reflections reach about 8–12x further.
   - Edge smoothing High is set to 512 instead of 8.
   - It saves some cost by turning off SSAO (ambient occlusion) and depth of field.
   - It doesn't load the stock Ts4CommonRules.sgr, so 42 options are missing from it. Config.log shows the game still falls back to working values.
3. **Two setter files in ConfigOverride are never loaded.** MySetters.sgr and SimpsSetters.sgr only work with the 2023 "setters" version of GraphicsRules.sgr, which sits in Simps_GraphicsRules_Setters and is not the active one. Simp4Sims' own "Ultimate Performance" preset uses B_Object_Cull 200 (the stock value), which shows 9999 is a quality setting.
4. **Options.ini is at Ultra or above for every graphics setting:** simquality 4, uncompressed sim textures 1, lightingquality 4, generalreflections 3, edgesmoothing 3, visualeffects 3, viewdistance 3, frameratelimit 240 with vsync off. Both fullscreen=1 and windowedfullscreen=1 are set, which is inconsistent. The graphics card has 5,920 MB of video memory (RTX 4050 Laptop).
5. **"Add culling": async culling is already on** (GameConfig.ini enableasyncculling=1). The game's exe lists only four settings in that section, so there is no hidden fast-load or culling switch there. The real culling improvements are removing the override and, if needed, lower View Distance or Object Quality.
6. **MC Command Center settings are almost all at defaults.** I compared mc_settings.cfg against the defaults stored in MCCC's own script code. The only population-related change is Population_RandomUseTraySimPercent 50 (default 0). Max sims in a zone is 20 (the default), and population and relationship culling are on.
7. **DQuiet_SimControlHub.json** holds 4 households with empty lists, so it has no performance effect.
8. **WickedWhims:** settings are stored per save. The newest profile uses WickedWhims' default activity preset: random activity multiplier 1.25, cooldown 100–1800, and activity starts when a lot loads. The older profiles use the calmer preset: 1.8, cooldown 900–3600, nothing started on lot load. All profiles have the window-peeper and creep features on (spawn chance 0.35 and 0.3), which bring extra NPCs onto the lot and can create new sims in the save. The WickedWhims log was replaced when the game was relaunched. Before that, I counted about 2,200 animation warnings and 28 errors during the 7/31 lot load.
9. **Other system points:**
   - C: has only 61 GB free (6.4%) and holds both the mods and the pagefile.
   - Windows Defender real-time scanning is on; I can't read its exclusions without admin rights.
   - The power plan is "Razer Cortex Power Plan".
   - Windows background game recording is on.
   - The game's online connection is stuck on "connecting" (ConnectionStatus.txt).
   - The GShade preset folder exists, but no ReShade/GShade files are in the game folder, so it costs nothing.
   - In Mods_parked\scripts, 20 variants of the Northern Siberia Winds lighting mod replace the same 4 data resources with up to 7 different versions, so only one of them can actually apply.

Suggested changes, in order (to be done by the user; nothing applied):
- Close Chrome, Brave, Discord and other Claude sessions before playing.
- Move ConfigOverride\GraphicsRules.sgr out of the folder (keep a backup) so the stock rules apply.
- In game: Sim Detail High, uncompressed sim textures off, Lighting High, Reflections Low, Edge Smoothing Low, Effects Medium, frame limit 60, and one display mode.
- Optionally set maxprotectedsims to 0 (80 protected sims instead of 150 in the rules files).
- Optionally set MCCC Max Sims in Zone to 15 and use the calmer WickedWhims preset.

All of these are in research\settings\proposed_settings.json.

claims.claim: The active ConfigOverride\GraphicsRules.sgr is the standalone Simp4Sims 'SGR Full 19-08-2021' ruleset, and it is actually loaded by the game.

loadorder.summary:
LOADORDER findings. Sources: web research plus static reverse-engineering of E:\The Sims 4\Game\Bin\TS4_x64.exe 1.126.73.1030 (capstone; addresses below are RVAs). I did not launch the game, so nothing here was confirmed in-game.
(a) Which copy wins. The higher Resource.cfg Priority number wins. The game's own cfgs show this: patch deltas ClientDeltaBuild* sit at -20 and override ClientFullBuild* at -30, and Mods default to 500, above all game data. Inside one Priority, the FIRST-loaded copy of a type/group/instance key is used and later copies are skipped. Scumbumbo showed this by in-game test (MTS t=604303, 2017) and his Conflict Detector 1.3.0 uses the same rule; he notes it is the reverse of earlier Sims games.
- Load order is one depth-first walk of Mods using raw FindFirstFileW/FindNextFileW with no sorting (walker 0x140d5e0 recurses at 0x140dfe1 inside its entry loop; its file-system vtable at 0x205a818 calls the FindFirstFileW/FindNextFileW wrappers). A sub-folder is loaded at the moment its name comes up, so folders and files are interleaved: Mods\AA\M.package loads before Mods\B.package, as Scumbumbo observed.
- On NTFS that order is upper-cased code-point order: '!' < digits (compared as text, so '10' < '9') < '@' < letters (case-insensitive) < '[' < '_' < '~'. Explorer shows '_' and '[' first, but in the game '_Overrides' and '[TS4]' names load LAST. Verified here with ntfs_order_demo.py.
- Folder depth and root-vs-subfolder only matter through this position. PackedFile line order does not change load order.
- '!!!' (e.g. NORTHERN SIBERIA WINDS: keep in the Mods root, don't rename) relies on first-wins, which is correct for TS4. 'zzz' relies on last-wins (older games), so in TS4 a zzz resource LOSES same-Priority conflicts. Only a higher Priority group wins regardless of names.
- One exception I did not verify: for Python script mods, whichever mod imports last patches last. So 'zzz' can still matter for script injections, if script import order follows the scan order.
(b) Resource.cfg. Parser at 0x140ef60 accepts only these keywords: Priority <int> (exactly one number, negatives allowed), PackedFile <pattern>, DirectoryFiles <pattern> [autoupdate], Group, FileType, Scan, StopScan, reset, and Select <cond> ... End.
- Paths are relative to the folder holding the cfg. Leading ./ is stripped; DirectoryFiles rejects ../ (PackedFile does not reject it; whether ../ works is untested).
- Wildcards are * and ?. A path segment of exactly '...' matches any depth, so 'PackedFile .../*.package' should load every depth (static reading only; Sims 3 used 'DirectoryFiles Files/... autoupdate').
- Literal folder names work (e.g. PackedFile animation/*.package), and multiple lines are fine. There is no exclusion keyword, but a package loads only if some pattern matches it, and folders no pattern matches are never entered. A level with only literal names is not even listed.
- If several patterns match one file, the file is registered once. The pattern with the fewest wildcard folder segments supplies its Priority; on a tie the earlier line wins. So 'Priority 1000 / PackedFile Overrides/*.package' beats '*/*.package' at 500 without loading the file twice (static reading).
- The walker also parses any Resource.cfg it finds in folders it enters (static; none exist in this library).
- The game writes the default cfg (Priority 500 plus 6 PackedFile lines, i.e. 5 sub-folder levels) only when the file is missing (0x150a90). The user's Mods\Resource.cfg is exactly that default.
- Scripts: the script scanner (0x14f580) ignores Resource.cfg. It is called on Mods with recurse=1 (0x150797) and then scans each sub-folder once with recurse=0. So .ts4script and .zip files (case-sensitive extension compare) load from the Mods root or one folder down only; Mods\<X>\Scripts\ folders of loose files are also added.
(c) Links. None of the code paths I checked filters NTFS reparse points: the walker, the script scanner, and the folder-exists test at 0x13ed030 (it only tests the directory bit 0x10). So links inside Mods should be followed. However, EA forum threads (13269809, 13282734) report that since the March 2026 patch a junctioned Mods or user folder is ignored. That is unverified and its cause is unknown, so the tools should not rely on junctions. Hard links work on this C: NTFS volume (tested) and look like ordinary files to the game.
(d) Size limits. The header check (0x13e7e20) reads the index position as 64-bit, requires the index to fit inside the file, requires entry count < 0x7FFFFFF and DBPF major version ≤ 2. The index reader (0x13e3540) reads each resource offset as an unsigned 32-bit value; the marker 0xFFFF0000 means a 64-bit offset follows, and size 0x3FFFFFFF means a 64-bit size follows. So the game itself has no 2 GiB limit; the ~4 GiB limit applies to normal entries, which is what third-party tools write.
- The '2 GB' merge cap is a Sims 4 Studio limit reported by users.
- The user's sim/125.package is 2,147,509,877 B, i.e. 26,229 B over 2^31. Its index starts at 0x7FFAF671 and crosses 2^31; all resource data ends below 2^31. The game should load it; some third-party tools may not.
- I found no cap on the number of packages. The '609 packages' anecdote from 2015 was a Wineskin/Mac setup.
Library check (Mods_parked treated as Mods): 617 packages load; 232,998 keys are duplicated across packages, and 19,029 of those have copies of different sizes. The biggest losers are sim/PRALINESIMS_MERGED (3,752 keys shadowed), sim/m3 (3,144) and sim/m22 (2,814). The biggest winners are sim/111, sim/103 and sim/116, because the unpadded numbers sort '1xx' before '30'..'99' and 'm*'. The 20 NORTHERN SIBERIA WINDS lighting variants all carry the same 4 SimData keys (type 0x545AC67A), so only '...AVERAGE BASE DARK ROOMS' is used.
Implications for the tools:
- The merger must pick duplicate winners in the game's walk order, and name its output so load order is kept.
- Keep merged packages ≤ 2^31 bytes so third-party tools can open them.
- Load profiles could be done by rewriting Mods\Resource.cfg with literal folder names instead of moving packages. Script mods still have to move: at 2+ folders deep they do not load.

claims.claim: At equal Resource.cfg Priority, the FIRST-loaded copy of a type/group/instance key is used; later duplicates are skipped (opposite of Sims 2/3).
claims.evidence: Scumbumbo, MTS 'Resource Load Order (Windows)' https://modthesims.info/t/604303 (12 Dec 2017, tested in-game with numbered conflicting packages); his TS4 Package Conflict Detector 1.3.0 notes 'the FIRST one loaded, not the last like previous versions' https://modthesims.info/d/572482 ; scumbumbo in https://modthesims.info/t/606443 (26 Jan 2018). The walk order found in the exe matches his observations.

claims.claim: The higher Priority number wins across groups; Mods (default 500) override all game data (negative priorities).
claims.evidence: E:\The Sims 4\Data\Client\Resource.cfg: ClientDeltaBuild* (patch deltas) at Priority -20 override ClientFullBuild* at -30; Delta\EP01\ResourceClient.cfg is the same; Data\Simulation\Resource.cfg: SimulationDeltaBuild0 -20 vs FullBuild0 -30. MTS Sims 3 wiki: 'higher priorities instructions override lower' https://modthesims.info/wiki.php?title=Sims_3%3AResource.cfg ; tested Overrides configs at 600/1000 https://modthesims.info/showthread.php?t=692264 (2025).

claims.claim: Load order within one Priority is a single depth-first walk in raw FindFirstFileW/FindNextFileW order (no sorting). A sub-folder is descended into when its name comes up, so folders and files are interleaved. On NTFS this is upper-cased code-point order: '!' < digits (not numeric) < '@' < A-Z (case-insensitive) < '[' < '_' < '~'. It differs from Explorer, where '_' and '[' come first.
claims.evidence: TS4_x64.exe RVA 0x140d5e0: the walker recurses at 0x140dfe1 inside the directory-entry loop and appends records in walk order. Its file-system vtable at RVA 0x205a818 calls 0x13f3a50/0x13f3e20, which wrap FindFirstFileW/FindNextFileW directly. research\loadorder\ntfs_order_demo.py output: !!!Lighting, !Dir/inner, 000_first, 10_x, 9_x, @at, AA/inner, aa_inner, Apple, apple2, b_dir/inner, Zeta, zzz/inner, zzz_Last, [TS4]thing, _Folder/inner, _Overrides, ~tilde.

claims.claim: The '!!!' prefix plus Mods-root placement (NORTHERN SIBERIA WINDS) makes a mod load near-first, so it wins same-priority conflicts. 'zzz' assumes last-wins and in TS4 makes the resource lose. '_Overrides' folders load LAST on NTFS, so they only work through a higher Priority group.
claims.evidence: Follows from the first-wins rule and the NTFS order demo. NSW instructions ('put directly in mods folder, do not rename, no subfolders'): https://www.patreon.com/northernsiberiawinds/posts/better-in-game-1-79174144 . Scumbumbo on older games using last-loaded-wins.

claims.claim: The Resource.cfg parser accepts only Priority <int> (exactly one argument, negatives allowed), PackedFile <pattern>, DirectoryFiles <pattern> [autoupdate], Group, FileType, Scan, StopScan, reset, Select <cond> ... End (with and/or/not). Paths must be relative and a leading ./ is stripped; DirectoryFiles rejects ../ but PackedFile does not (untested).
claims.evidence: Parser at RVA 0x140ef60 references the strings StopScan(0x140f4ca), Group, reset, Priority(0x140f7d8, 'cmp esi,2'), FileType, Scan, DirectoryFiles(0x140fcc1, creates instruction type 1 id 0x34728492, 'autoupdate' sets +0x14), PackedFile(0x140fe5b, type 1 id 0x2a43bd44), Select(0x140ffe0), End. Wildcard tokens '?*' and '.../' are at file offset 0x2058d80.

claims.claim: PackedFile patterns can name literal folders (e.g. 'PackedFile animation/*.package'), and multiple lines are allowed. '*' and '?' are wildcards, and a whole segment '...' matches any depth. There is no exclusion keyword, but only matched folders are entered, and levels with only literal names are not listed at all.
claims.evidence: Walker 0x140d5e0: segments split on \ / : ; wcspbrk(seg,'?*') or seg=='...' sets the enumerate flag. Without it, the literal branch at 0x140e28e checks existence directly and recurses. It recurses into a sub-directory only if the new pattern list is non-empty (0x140dfd2). The file stage accepts a pending '...' segment (0x140e054). The game's own cfgs use literal names (ClipHeader.package, UI*.package). Community Overrides/*.package configs report working (MTS t=692264).

claims.claim: When several PackedFile lines match the same file, it is registered once, using the pattern with the fewest wildcard/'...' folder segments; on a tie the earlier line wins. So 'Priority 1000 / PackedFile Overrides/*.package' beats '*/*.package' at 500 regardless of line order.
claims.evidence: Walker file stage 0x140e015-0x140e0b0 keeps the minimum (depth counter at entry+0x18, wildcard counter at entry+0x1a) starting from 1000/1000, replacing only on strictly smaller values (jl/jge). The wildcard counter is incremented only for wildcard or '...' segments (0x140df9f / 0x140dd60).

claims.claim: While walking, the game parses any Resource.cfg found in folders it enters (nested cfgs add instructions).
claims.evidence: At the start of walker 0x140d5e0 (0x140d670-0x140d6ae): for each configured cfg name it builds dir+name, calls the file-exists vtable slot, then calls the parser 0x140ef60. MTS Sims 3 wiki: PackedFile/DirectoryFiles 'look for additional Resource.cfg files in every directory'. No stray Resource.cfg exists in Mods or Mods_parked (find).

claims.claim: The game writes the default Mods\Resource.cfg (Priority 500 plus PackedFile *.package ... */*/*/*/*/*.package, i.e. 5 sub-folder levels) only when the file is missing. The user's current file is exactly this default.
claims.evidence: The template strings are in TS4_x64.exe at file offset 0x1e17b78. Function RVA 0x150a90: dir-exists 0x13ed030, file-exists 0x13ed2f0 at 0x150d95, skip-if-present jne at 0x150d9c, 7 write-line calls at 0x150e96-0x150f3e. The user's Mods\Resource.cfg was read.

claims.claim: Script mods are found by a separate scanner that ignores Resource.cfg. It picks up .ts4script and .zip files in the Mods root and in first-level sub-folders only (extension compare looks case-sensitive), plus Mods\<X>\Scripts\ loose folders. Scripts 2+ folders deep never load.
claims.evidence: RVA 0x150797 calls 0x14f580(this, ModsPath, recurse=1). For a directory it tests <X>\Scripts\ (0x14f779/0x14f81f), then calls itself with recurse=0 (0x14fa2d); with recurse=0 directories are skipped (0x14f63e). Extension compare against '.zip'/'.ts4script' via case-sensitive wcscmp 0x13c9620 (0x14faae/0x14fac1). Python side: core.zip paths.USER_SCRIPT_ROOTS is filled from native code. EA forum rule: https://forums.ea.com/discussions/the-sims-4-mods-and-custom-content-en/sub-folders/9164012

claims.claim: The TS4 1.126 folder walkers do not filter NTFS reparse points, so junctions and symlinks inside Mods should be followed like normal folders. But EA forum reports say that since the March 2026 patch a junctioned Mods folder (or whole user folder) is ignored. Cause unknown; do not rely on junctions.
claims.evidence: The directory-entry code (0x13f3c6e) tests only attribute bit 0x10; dir-exists 0x13ed030 tests 'al & 0x10'; no mitigation-policy or reparse APIs are imported. Reports: https://forums.ea.com/discussions/the-sims-4-technical-issues-pc-en/directory-junctions-for-mods-folder-no-longer-functioning-after-recent-update/13282734 and .../game-no-longer-reads-user-folder-on-external-drive-junction-broken/13269809 (EA forum pages return 403; content taken from search snippets).

claims.claim: NTFS hard links work on this machine's C: volume and look like ordinary files (no reparse bit), so they are a safe way to share one library copy between profiles on the same volume.
claims.evidence: os.link test in research\loadorder: nlink=2, attributes 0x20, reparse bit clear. C: and E: are NTFS fixed drives (Get-Volume).

claims.claim: The game's DBPF reader has no 2 GiB limit: header index position is 64-bit and checked against the 64-bit file size; normal entry offsets are unsigned 32-bit (about 4 GiB); an EA-only escape allows 64-bit offsets and sizes. Entry count must be < 0x7FFFFFF and major version ≤ 2. The '2 GB' cap is a Sims 4 Studio limit.
claims.evidence: 0x13e7e20: cmp 'DBPF'; version ≤ 2; [0x24] < 0x7FFFFFF; mov rcx,[rbx+0x40] (qword) < filesize; +[0x2c] ≤ filesize; [0x3c] != 0. Reader 0x13e3540: 'mov eax,[rbx+4]' (zero-extended); cmp eax,0xFFFF0000 → reads 8-byte offset; size==0x3FFFFFFF → reads 8-byte size. Writer 0x13e3a00 emits the same escapes. S4S 2 GB merge cap per forum search results (sims4studio.com/thread/13712).

dupes.summary:
I hashed every stored copy of every resource key that appears more than once: 249,703 keys, 659,859 copies, 80.38 GB read from NVMe in 105 s. Where copies differed, I decompressed them and compared the unpacked bytes.

**How the duplicates split**
- 226,221 keys are byte-identical in every copy.
- 3,408 more keys hold the same content and differ only in compression.
- 20,074 keys really conflict. One of these is the Sims 4 Studio (S4S) merge-manifest key and one is the NameMap key, which are tool metadata, so about 20,072 are real conflicts.
- 0 keys were undecidable.
- 14 copies could not be decompressed. They are 7 corrupt eyebrow textures, each stored in both sim/111.package and sim/PRALINESIMS_MERGED.package.

**What deduplication would save**
- Keeping one copy of each identical key removes 355,762 copies and 45.32 GB. That is 17.5% of the 258.9 GB library, or 91.9 GB uncompressed.
- Keeping one copy of every duplicated key (the copy the game would load) removes 409,992 copies (17.3% of all index entries) and 46.73 GB.
- CAS parts: the library has 755,662 copies of 614,076 distinct CAS parts, so 141,586 are extra. Removing identical ones drops 102,269. The other 39,317 belong to 15,533 conflicting CAS parts.
- 86% of the identical extra copies come from the same original CC file merged into several merged packages. I found this by reading all 165 S4S merge manifests; 3,421 source files appear in 2 or more merges.

**Packages that are completely redundant**
- 87 packages (37.85 GB) contain nothing that does not also exist identically in another package. 16 of them are the big ~2 GB merges.
- 66 of them (30.17 GB, including 13 big merges and 125.package) can be removed together. Every content version and every copy the game would load stays in place.
- If the NameMap is also ignored, the figures are 101 redundant packages (38.45 GB), of which 82 (30.77 GB) are removable together.

**What the conflicts are**
- Mostly different versions of the same CC file inside the sim/ merges: 19,227 conflicting keys sit only in sim/, and 12,100 have the same source name in every copy.
- When a conflicting CAS part keeps the same size, the difference is at most 8 bytes, almost always the catalog sort-priority value.
- Neither the bigger copy nor the newer file date tells you which copy the game picks. The CAS part format version (the first 4 bytes) is a better guide.

**Script-mod tuning sitting inside CC merges**
- sim/m27 holds an older copy of TURBODRIVER_WickedWhims_Tuning.
- sim/m9 holds lot51_plumbbros.
- FallenCore_Tunings is inside four merges and the chingyu traits inside three.

**Problems in the Mods folder the game loads now**
- 752 MB are identical extra copies.
- WW_LAMABOY_Animations.package is a near-copy of WW_LAMABOY_Animation.package.
- Several WickedWhims animation-list resources are overridden by a much smaller copy inside anim1, anim2 or anim3.

**125.package**
- All its resources lie below the 2^31-byte (2 GiB) mark. Only the last 26,229 bytes of its index are past it.
- No EA game package reaches 2 GiB, so how the game handles a file this large is untested.
- The package is fully redundant, so it can simply be left out.

Who wins a conflict is based on one 2017 community test (scumbumbo): the first-loaded copy wins, with folders searched depth-first in alphabetical order. I did not check this in-game.

lagdrivers.summary:
LAGDRIVERS: what drives TS4 load time and lag with this library, and which fixes are real. Everything was measured read-only on this machine unless marked as coming from the web.
WHAT THE LIBRARY IS: nearly all CAS. There are 614,076 unique CAS parts (755,662 CASP entries). The whole game with every pack has 111,481 unique CASPs, so the CC is 5.5x the game's CAS catalog. There are only 3,037 OBJD objects. Of the 258.9 GB, textures and meshes make up about 95% (RLE2 147.8 GB, LRLE 49.0 GB, GEOM 40.4 GB). CASPs are only 0.34 GB on disk (0.52 GB inflated). There are also 26,359 XML tuning files (259 MB) and 2,256 script-mod Python modules (14.9 MB). The game itself has 3,265 modules; WickedWhims alone has 1,133.
LOAD TIME DEPENDS ON ITEM COUNT, NOT GB: reading the index of all 624 packages (2.36M entries, 75.7 MB) took 1.34 s cold and 0.76 s warm. Reading and inflating every CASP in single-threaded Python took 265 s cold and 102 s warm. The game is C++ and faster per item, but its work still grows with the number of CAS parts, tuning files and script modules. Texture bytes are only loaded when needed.
STARTUP STAGES: the exe has a stage list (ResourceSystem, ModManagerService, PreloadAllResources, Catalog InitLoad/IncrementalLoad, TuningLoaded, SimInfoSystem, Complete). Lot loading screens are about 40 Python zone spin-up states, including _LoadHouseholdsAndSimInfos, _SpawnSims and _PrerollAutonomy. Since the July 21 2026 patch, EA fully starts Python before the main menu. EA says a vanilla start should take 1-2 minutes.
"LOAD IN SECONDS" WITH HUNDREDS OF GB: impossible if everything is installed. The only real lever is loading less: profiles, a lean "used CC" pack, and removing the 141k duplicate CASP copies.
BIGGEST FINDING, THE GRAPHICS OVERRIDE: ConfigOverride\GraphicsRules.sgr is Simp4Sims "19-08-2021 SGR Full" (Config.log lines 1-2). It does not include SimpsSetters.sgr, so MySetters.sgr and the presets do nothing. It also replaces EA's current Ts4CommonRules.sgr with 2021 copies. It turns off the game's own culling and LOD:
- Sim LOD distances go from 25/50/100/1000 to 2999.97-3000, so every Sim renders at full detail.
- Sim textures are 2048 at every LOD (stock drops to 1024/512/128).
- ObjectSizeCullFactor goes from 200 to 9999 (small-object culling effectively off).
- The far clip goes from 1000/1500 to 9999.
- ObjectLODBias goes from 0.6666 to 0.
- Shadow maps go from 2048 to 5120 and the anti-aliasing level from 8 to 512.
- TextureSizeThreshold goes from 1024 to 4096.
So the fastest "culling" win is to remove this override (stock rules) or use the Setters version with the Ultimate Performance preset. That preset keeps ObjectSizeCullFactor at 200.
CULLING IN THE GAME: rendering is C++. The exe has OcclusionQuery classes, ObjectSizeCullFactor and an EnableAsyncCulling early setting (the user already has it on in GameConfig.ini). Python mods cannot change rendering; they can only hide or fade individual objects. The simulation has its own "culling":
- Sims off-lot run at reduced detail (SimInfoLODLevel).
- Save population caps: SIM_INFO_CAP and a "firemeter" that purges Sims over the cap.
- Story-progression removal of Sims and old relationships.
- The Max Sims option (80/150/200/Unlimited; Maxis says 150 is fine on mid-high PCs and advises against 200/Unlimited).
- An NPC soft cap. MCCC's "Max Sims in Zone" (default 20) calls the same game function; MCCC also changes walkby counts and has Bypass Culling. Turning culling off makes lag worse.
IN-GAME LAG DRIVERS FOUND HERE:
- CC textures are 4x the game's size: 55% of sampled CC CAS textures are 2048x4096 and some are 4096x8192. All of the game's own are 1024x2048. The game builds a Sim's skin-and-clothes texture at 2048 anyway, so the extra detail is probably thrown away while the 4x decode and memory cost is not.
- The machine is tight: a 6 GB laptop GPU, uncompressed Sim textures on, 16 GB RAM, and only 306 MB free RAM when the game started on Sep 23.
- Error spam: 93 exception reports in one session on Jul 31, and a 4.2 MB Fallen exception log.
LAG-FIX MODS: they treat symptoms. Simulation Unclogger (TURBODRIVER) resets Sims stuck in repeated actions. Simulation Lag Fix (SrslySims, now retired) changes game time speeds; Simulation Flow Unleashed (AveryPing) replaces it. TwistedMexi has no performance mod; Better Exceptions is a diagnostic tool.
CACHE FILES (Crinrict, Aug 2025):
- Delete localthumbcache after adding or removing CC.
- Can delete: localsimtexturecache (100 MB cap; it speeds up Sim loading), avatarcache, cachestr, onlinethumbnailcache, Events.ini, lastException files.
- Keep: accountDataDB, notify.glob, UserSetting.ini, Options.ini, content, ConfigOverride.
- Deleting ReticulatedSplinesView brings back all the "new" stars.
- None of these make startup faster.
LAUNCH FLAGS: strings found in TS4_x64.exe: nointro, -nopreload, -no_tutorial, -show_tutorial, -forcepack, -nosound, -disableCrashReporter, -fullMemoryDump, -noupnp, -data, -shareddata, -effects, -trial, -l <locale>. There is no -noautoload. What they do is untested because I could not launch the game.
MYTH vs FACT:
(1) "The game scans all 259 GB every launch." FACT: it reads the package indexes, about 1 s here.
(2) "GB is what matters." FACT: the number of CAS parts, tuning files and script modules is what matters.
(3) "Merging makes it load much faster." FACT: file count is not the bottleneck (624 files load in about 1 s), and merging does not reduce item count. S4S staff: "Merging will absolutely not fix the conflicts."
(4) "Deleting caches speeds up loading." FACT: it fixes stale thumbnails; it does not speed up startup.
(5) "Simp's SGR makes the game smoother." FACT: the active SGR Full file makes it heavier.
(6) "A mod can add render culling." FACT: no. Only GraphicsRules settings and in-game options can.
(7) "Lag-fix mods remove lag." FACT: they only fix stuck Sims and slowed time.
(8) "No More Culling / Bypass Culling is good for performance." FACT: it is the opposite.
(9) "CC doesn't use RAM because the game only loads pointers." FACT: the CAS catalog and every worn 4K texture cost memory.
(10) "-nointro or -noautoload speeds up loading." FACT: no -noautoload exists, and skipping intro logos saves seconds at most (not verified).
(11) "Loading in seconds with 500 GB." FACT: impossible without loading less.
NOTE: TS4_x64.exe was running from 23:52:52 while I worked, launched by someone else with the lean Mods set. After about 6 min it used 3.9 GB private memory. My cold benchmark overlapped that run.

merging.summary:
MERGING research. Everything here was checked on this machine. Nothing under the Sims 4 Documents folder or E:\The Sims 4 was written. The game was not launched.

(1) S4S manifest, fully decoded
- Type 0x7FB6AD8A is the FNV-1 32-bit hash of "s4smergedpackagemanifest". Evidence is S4S's own class S4Studio.Data.IO.Package.S4SMergedPackageManifest; its .cctor computes FNV.Hash32 of that name. I read the bytecode (IL) of S4S 3.2.6.3 installed on this PC. Nothing was executed, and the EULA has no clause against reverse engineering.
- Layout: `u32 version=1` + FOLDER.
  - FOLDER = `u32 nameLen` + UTF-8 name + `u32 folderCount` + FOLDER[] + `u32 packageCount` + PACKAGE[].
  - PACKAGE = `u32 nameLen` + UTF-8 name (no ".package") + `i32 count` + count × (`u64 instance`, `u32 type`, `u32 group`).
  - In a flat merge the root name is "" and there are 0 subfolders. That is why a hex dump looks like "01000000 00000000 00000000 count".
- My decoder/encoder is s4s_manifest.py. It rebuilds all 165 manifests in the library byte for byte. All 165 use key 7FB6AD8A:0:0, zlib compression, and sit at offset 96. Together they list 36,758 source packages and 2,393,908 keys.

(4) Do fewer, bigger packages load faster?
- Only the per-file overhead changes. EA itself loads 5,080 packages holding 4,855,988 resources; the mods add 624 files (+12%) but 2,364,302 resources (+49%).
- My benchmark of 2,000 packages vs 1 merged package:

  - 0.13–0.22 ms per file with a warm cache;

verdicts.claim: 1. At equal Priority the FIRST-loaded copy of a T/G/I key wins; later duplicates are skipped
verdicts.reason: The primary sources say what the claim says. Scumbumbo ran an in-game test with numbered conflicting packages (MTS t/604303, 12 Dec 2017), and his Conflict Detector 1.3.0 changelog (11 Dec 2017) says 'the FIRST one loaded, not the last like previous versions'. The NSW '!!!' naming and 'do not rename, no subfolders' instruction is recent indirect support. Every 'last loaded wins / add ZZZ' statement I found is Sims 2/3 material or untested folklore (MTS t=478024, TheSimsTree blog). Caveats: Scumbumbo's own 26 Jan 2018 post limits it to 'XML mods in Windows OS, this may not hold true for CC or Macs'. Nobody has re-tested it on 1.126. The exe disassembly confirms the walk order but not the key-resolution rule itself. Not verified on this machine.
verdicts.evidence: Fetched MTS t/604303 (the first post quotes 'The FIRST resource loaded is the one used by the game'), MTS d/572482 changelog 1.3.0, MTS t/606443 (scumbumbo, 26 Jan 2018, with the XML/Windows caveat).

verdicts.claim: 2. The higher Priority number wins across groups; Mods at 500 override the game's negative-priority data
verdicts.reason: I read the game's cfgs. Data\Client\Resource.cfg puts ClientDeltaBuild* at -20 above ClientFullBuild* at -30. Data\Simulation\Resource.cfg has SimulationDeltaBuild0 at -20 and FullBuild0 at -30. Delta\EP01\ResourceClient.cfg and ResourceSimulation.cfg use the same scheme, plus Strings_* at -9. Patches could not work unless higher numbers win. Community Overrides configs at 600/1000 are reported to work (MTS t=692264, Simz4Fun, 29 Aug 2025). 'All game data' goes further than anyone has tested, but I found no counterexample. The cited Sims 3 wiki is second-hand for TS4.

verdicts.claim: 3. Within one Priority the load order is a single depth-first FindFirstFileW/FindNextFileW walk with no sorting and folders interleaved with files; on NTFS this is upper-cased ordinal order
verdicts.reason: I re-disassembled it. Vtable 0x205a818 slot +0x18 is 0x140ea90, which jumps to 0x13f3a50 (FindFirstFileW at 0x13f3c45). Slot +0x20 is 0x140eab0, which jumps to 0x13f3e20 (FindNextFileW at 0x13f3e41). These are streaming wrappers that store the name at +2 and the directory flag (attr>>4 &1) at +0x20a. The walker checks +0x20a and recurses (0x140dfe1) before it calls FindNext (0x140e1e1). There is no buffering or sort. I ran a copy of ntfs_order_demo.py on C: and got exactly the order quoted in the claim, and os.scandir order equals FindFirstFileW order. This matches Scumbumbo's 'subfolders are visited in order as the folder is processed'. One gap: I did not check whether a later stage re-sorts records within a priority. Scumbumbo's 2017 test suggests it does not. NTFS order is not contractually guaranteed, and FAT/exFAT drives return directory-entry order instead.
verdicts.evidence: research\loadorder_review\rdis.py (vt 205a818, 13f3e20); ntfs_demo_copy.py output identical to the claim.

verdicts.claim: 4. A '!!!' prefix in the Mods root loads near-first and wins; a 'zzz' prefix loses; '_Overrides' loads last on NTFS, so it only works through a higher Priority
verdicts.reason: This follows from claims 1 and 3 and the NTFS demo: '_' (0x5F) sorts after all digits and letters. Correction: '_' is not strictly last. Names starting with '`', '{', '|', '}', '~' or non-ASCII characters sort after it, and a name starting with a space or a longer run of '!' sorts before '!!!['. The NSW 'do not change the name and do not put the file in subfolders' instruction is confirmed by the CurseForge/Patreon search snippet. The Patreon page itself returns 403.

verdicts.claim: 5. The Resource.cfg keyword set: Priority <int>, PackedFile, DirectoryFiles [autoupdate], Group, FileType, Scan, StopScan, reset, Select...End

verdicts.claim: 6. PackedFile patterns can name literal folders; '*', '?' and '...' are supported; there is no exclusion keyword but only matched folders are entered
verdicts.reason: Walker 0x140d9a0-0x140da51 splits segments on \ / : and flags a segment that contains '?*' (0x205a58c) or equals '.../' (0x205a580). It takes the literal branch (0x140e28e) when no segment is flagged, and recurses only when the child pattern list is non-empty (0x140dfd2). EA's long-standing '5 folders deep' rule is empirical proof that unmatched folders are not loaded. Caveats: '...' (any depth) has only static support in TS4; it is documented Sims 3 syntax. I don't know what the 'Scan'/'StopScan' keywords do, so 'no exclusion keyword' is not proven. The key builder use, a cfg that lists only some folders as a load profile, has not been tested in-game. It never affects script mods (see claim 10).

verdicts.claim: 7. A file matched by several PackedFile lines is registered once, using the pattern with the fewest wildcard folder segments; ties go to the earlier line
verdicts.reason: The file stage 0x140e015-0x140e0b0 takes the minimum over instruction-type-1 entries. The primary key is word entry+0x18, which increments on every descent (0x140df8e). The secondary key is word entry+0x1a, which increments only when the segment is flagged as wildcard (0x140df9f-0x140dfaa). It starts from 1000/1000 and replaces only on a strictly smaller value, so ties keep the earlier entry. One record is then created from the chosen instruction (0x140e0d3-0x140e1bd). Community Overrides configs place the 600/1000 block AFTER the default 500 block and report that it works (MTS t=692264), which fits 'regardless of line order'. The tie-break on equal wildcard counts is static-only.

verdicts.claim: 11. The walkers do not filter reparse points, so junctions are followed, but since the March 2026 patch a junctioned Mods or user folder reportedly fails; no reparse or mitigation APIs are imported
verdicts.reason: Correct part: the directory test uses only attribute bit 0x10 (0x13f3e6b-0x13f3e74), and the exe contains no SetProcessMitigationPolicy or RedirectionTrust strings. Wrong part: the exe DOES import GetFinalPathNameByHandleW. It is used at 0x12a6429 and 0x12a6480 inside function 0x12a61d0, which opens a path with CreateFileW, resolves the final (link-followed) path and passes it to PathGetDriveNumberW, so the game can learn a link's real drive letter. I found nothing that refutes the core model. What a builder should believe:

1. **Load order and conflict winners.** Within one Priority, packages load in a depth-first FindFirstFileW walk: NTFS upper-cased ordinal order, with folders entered at the point their name comes up. When two copies of a key conflict, the first-loaded one wins. This rule was proven in-game only for XML tuning, on Windows, in 2017. Before shipping anything that decides CC winners, re-test it on 1.126 with two conflicting CAS parts; it takes minutes.

2. **Priority.** A higher Priority beats a lower one. A more specific pattern (fewer wildcard folder segments) takes over a file from the default `*/*.package` lines regardless of line order.

3. **Folder names.** `_` sorts after letters and digits but is not strictly last: backtick, `{`, `~` and non-ASCII names come after it.

4. **Resource.cfg profiles.** The only empirical proof that folders not matched by patterns are skipped is the depth limit ("5 folders deep"). Name-based skipping and `...` are supported by static reading only, so test in-game before relying on them. A Resource.cfg profile never disables script mods. Scripts load from the Mods root and first-level folders whatever Resource.cfg says, so a profile that hides a folder of packages can leave its script loaded without its companion package. Handle scripts by moving them, never by cfg.

5. **Nested Resource.cfg.** Treat nested Resource.cfg files as live (unconfirmed, but the safe assumption). The tool should flag stray ones and never write one inside subfolders. There are none today.

6. **Merged package size.** Keep merged packages below 2^31 bytes including the index. Game support above 2 GiB rests on static reading only, and 125.package does not test it. Other tools may use signed 32-bit offsets. The S4S 2 GB cap is lore; the cited S4S thread does not say it.

The cause of the 2026 reports is still unknown. The exe here also imports a non-EA DLL ('anadius64'), so EA-app user reports may not transfer. Hard links on the same NTFS volume are safe, but only on C:. Beware of tools that edit files in place.

I checked every claim and ran Sims 4 Studio 3.2.6.3's own merge and unmerge code on synthetic files in research/merging_review2 only. Nothing under the Sims 4 Documents folder or E:\The Sims 4 was written.

**The library index is out of date.** Files have moved since library.sqlite was built. For example, Mods/animation/anim1.package is gone and research/merging/s4s_manifest.py --selftest now crashes. Tools must look up each package by root, then the other root, and check the size (see research/merging_review2/resolve.py). Better still, rebuild the index before any merge.

**The manifest format and unmerge rules are safe to build on.**
- Format: u32 version, then the recursive folder / package / (instance, type, group) layout.
- Write one manifest per package, key 7FB6AD8A:0:0, zlib compressed, first in the file. S4S does not check the version and does not care about its position or compression.
- Every resource must be listed under exactly the name you want back.
- Names within a folder must be unique ignoring case. S4S compares names case-sensitively but writes files with File.Create, so 'X' and 'x' become one file.
- Names must be sanitised: no path separators, no '..', no drive letters. S4S builds output paths with Path.Combine and would write outside the target folder.
- Never put any other resource of type 0x7FB6AD8A into a package. S4S treats any resource of that type as the manifest, and a bad one makes it refuse the package.

**S4S merge behaviour.**
- For a key in several sources, the first copy is kept but every source still lists it. Unmerging then gives each source the winner's bytes, so the losing originals cannot be recovered.
- Duplicate keys inside one source are all written.
- There is no filtering by resource type. Source manifests are skipped only because their key clashes with the new one.
- The 2 GB check only runs when merging. Opening and unmerging have no size limit.

**Unmerge loss in the existing 165 merged packs:**

| Outcome | Packages |
|---|---|
| Fully lossless | 25 |
| Lose only S4S's batch-fix history record (0x6BF15BBE) | 125 |
| Drop real content (12,610 resources) | 36, not the claimed 142 |
| List keys that are missing (12,358 keys) | 19 |

The dropped content is mostly animation clip headers and clips, plus 1,726 textures converted from RLE2 to LRLE after merging.

**Which duplicate wins in-game.** The best evidence (scumbumbo, tested in-game in 2017) says the first-loaded copy wins, and the project's winners.py already assumes this. It is still unconfirmed on game version 1.126. Keep excluding or isolating packages whose copies differ, because merging moves every resource to the merged file's position in the load order.

**Startup cost per file is underestimated.** 0.13-0.59 ms/file is the best case for raw file reads. I measured about 8 ms/file when Windows Defender (or something like it) scans a file on first open, and 10 ms/file on one cold pass over older files. The Steam test implies about 9 ms/file in-game even on a warm second run. Use 0.5-10 ms/file (roughly 0.3-6 s for this 624-file library), not a fixed 0.2 s.

**EA's 5,080 packages** include 4,035 string-table packages in 18 languages, loaded by a wildcard in Resource.cfg. Whether the game opens all of them is unverified, so comparisons of mod file count against EA file count are weak.

**Size cap.** To stay within what EA itself ships, keep merged packs at or below about 1.98e9 bytes (1.85 GiB), not 1.9 GiB. The reason to stay under 2^31-1 is that S4S can then still add to or re-merge the pack, not that it could not open or unmerge it. How the game handles packages over 2 GiB is untested. sim/125.package only goes over because of its index table.

**Other tools and figures.**
- s4pi-reforged: only use it on flat merges. It keeps the last duplicate and drops EA's 0x73E93EEB XML manifests.
- Companion classification is heuristic. Treat 'weak' and 'orphan' packages as never-merge; UI_Cheats_Extension.package, for example, is only rated 'weak'. The 46 script-bearing merged packs total 66.8 GB, not 67.5 GB.
- Claims 11-14, 16 and 17 hold as stated.

1. Package indexes are not the problem. Reading all 624 indexes takes 0.06-0.34 s.

profiler.summary:
An in-game lag profiler that attributes simulation time to script mods is feasible on this build (game Python 3.7.0, python37_x64.dll, build string "Apr 10 2025, MSC v.1916 64 bit"). I tested everything on this machine by loading the game's own python37_x64.dll into a small test program (research/profiler/host37.py). The program starts Python the same way Simulation_x64.dll does and never releases the GIL, just like the game. The game itself was not launched, so in-game behaviour is still unconfirmed.

(a) How script mods are loaded. C++ scans Mods: TS4_x64.exe has the strings 'Mods\', '.ts4script', '.zip' and 'Scripts' at 0x1e17b30-0x1e17b68, next to 'ScriptModsEnabled' and the 'PackedFile */*/*/*/*/*.package' patterns. Simulation_x64.dll imports PySys_SetPath and calls the Python functions sims4.importer.utils.import_modules / import_modules_by_path (core.zip, lines 26 and 104). The Python helper module_names_gen only lists '.+\.py[co]$' files inside .zip/.ts4script archives, and only '.py' files in loose folders. I ran the game's own code on Cumshine.ts4script and it returned [], so its Spent_Cumshine.py is never imported. None of the 18,567 tuning resources I scanned refer to that module, so the mod does nothing as shipped. zipimport itself can import .py source by name (tested), and the game's CustomFinder puts no .pyc-only limit on imports. For modules loaded from a zip, __file__ is '<archive>\<inner path>', but co_filename keeps the author's build path (tested).

(b) What the game's Python provides. It has 63 built-in modules, including _thread, _lsprof, time, faulthandler, _tracemalloc, zipimport and sys. sys._current_frames, setprofile, settrace, perf_counter (QueryPerformanceCounter, 100 ns resolution) and thread_time all exist. threading, cProfile and pstats import and work. ctypes, asyncio and sqlite3 are not available. The default GIL switch interval is 5 ms. Simulation_x64.dll imports 189 Python functions and none of them release the GIL (no PyEval_SaveThread or PyGILState_*). So the simulation thread holds the GIL all the time. Other Python threads only run while it is executing Python code, or during a GIL-releasing call such as sleep or I/O.

(c) Main loop entry points in this version. C++ calls areaserver.c_api_server_tick(absolute_ticks). That calls Zone.update(absolute_ticks), which calls TimeService.update(time_slice=True). That runs sim_timeline.simulate with max_time_ms=MAX_TIME_SLICE_MILLISECONDS (default 50 ms), then Timeline.simulate(until, max_elements=10000, max_time_ms=None), then each element's _run or _resume. Other entry points:
- Alarms: AlarmElement._run(self, t) and RepeatingAlarmElement._run(self, t) call self.callback(handle).
- Events: EventManagerService.process_event(event_type, sim_info=None, **kwargs) leads to handler.handle_event.
- Autonomy: AutonomyService._update_gen(timeline), which yields after MAX_SECONDS_PER_LOOP (default 1/30 s).
- Interactions: InteractionQueue.process_one_interaction_gen(timeline).

(d) Cheat commands and notifications. Use sims4.commands.Command(*aliases, command_type=CommandType.Live), where Live=5. Write console output with sims4.commands.CheatOutput(_connection). Show a notification with ui.ui_dialog_notification.UiDialogNotification.TunableFactory().default(None, title=..., text=...).show_dialog(), using sims4.localization.LocalizationHelperTuning.get_raw_text for the text. For auto-stop, use alarms.add_alarm_real_time with clock.interval_in_real_seconds.

(e) Mapping code to the owning mod. co_filename values are author paths, for example 'E:\Builds\MCCC_2026_4_0\...', '.\WickedWhims_v185k\...', 'E:\\\\Python3_7_0\\\\version_vault\\...', '/Users/a/Sims/...' and 'lot51_core/tags.pyc'. EA's own code is 'T:\InGame\Gameplay\Scripts\...' and 'D:\dev\TS4\_deploy\...'. Inside the game, frame.f_globals['__file__'] is the most reliable way to find the owner. It works even for MCCC archives that hold 17 top-level modules. When only a filename is available, a map from co_filename to archive covers 27,235 code objects and 2,245 file names. Only one name is ambiguous: '__init__.py', shared by 3 LittleMsSam mods.

Measured on the game's own Python 3.7 in the test program:
- Python sampler thread (sys._current_frames): unreliable. It only gets the GIL when the main thread runs Python code, so code at the start of each Python burst is under-sampled. Shares were off by 5-16 points (for example 33.5/19.6/46.9 when the true split was 50/12.5/37.5). Switch intervals below 1 ms make the two threads keep handing the GIL back and forth.
- faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(repeat=True) as a sampler: accurate. It samples without the GIL and writes to a file; I parse the file after the run. Result: 49.4/13.6/37.0 against a true 50/12.5/37.5, at about 62 samples/s, with no measurable slowdown. Small caveat: it reads stacks while the game is running.
- External memory reader (extsampler.py): read the test program's memory from a separate process. It came within 0.5 points on longer runs (39.5/20.2/40.2 against 39.8/20/40) and correctly split time spent inside vs outside Python (32.2% measured vs 33.7% true). It adds nothing inside the game and can profile loading screens.
- cProfile: cut throughput by about 44%.
- Exact timers around alarm callbacks: accurate to the millisecond.

Recommendation: use the external reader plus an optional in-game mod. The mod (prototype at ts4prof_proto/ts4prof.py, which works in the test program) uses the faulthandler sampler, exact timers on alarm callbacks and Zone.update, and the game's simulator-debt value. Still to check in-game: sys.path contents (whether each .ts4script is its own entry); whether C++ caches the areaserver.c_api_server_tick function object (the design wraps Zone.update, which is safe either way); whether sims4.importer.custom_import.enable() and macros.c_api_register_global_importer are active in retail. The last one only matters for importing .py source.

Can the external reader open TS4_x64.exe with PROCESS_VM_READ as the same user without admin, and does the EA App or any anti-tamper block it? It worked against the test program, but the game itself is untested.

Does the simulation (Python) thread differ from the render thread? The client/server naming (c_api_server_tick, distributor) suggests Python lag shows up as simulator debt (sims standing still) rather than lower FPS, but this is unconfirmed. The external reader's time-outside-Python figure plus a thread list would settle it.

How safe is faulthandler's GIL-free stack reading under EA's custom allocators (Py_RegisterMemoryHooks / PyObject_SetArenaAllocator / PPMalloc)? A rare crash is possible if a frame is freed mid-read. Needs soak testing in-game before making it the default.
What timer resolution does TS4 actually request with timeBeginPeriod? This only affects the Python sampler thread's rate. On Windows 11, minimized or hidden windows can lose high timer resolution.

Real TS4 stacks are deeper (possibly 60-150 frames) and Python bursts are more irregular than in the synthetic test. The Python sampler thread's bias may be smaller in real play; compare it against the external reader in one real session.

The in-game map from module name to mod assumes mods are imported on the main thread, with MAIN_TID captured at import. Mods that exec code with custom globals lacking __file__ would be counted as 'game'. The co_filename map can be used as a fallback.

usedcc.summary:
USEDCC: which CC do the user's sims and lots actually use? (Everything here was measured on this machine. Nothing under the Sims 4 user folder or E:\The Sims 4 was written to, and the game was not launched.)

(a) CASP 0x034AEECB layout, verified. The uint32 at offset 4 plus 8 gives the absolute start of the TGI list. The list is a uint8 count, then count x 16 bytes in I-G-T order (uint64 instance, uint32 group, uint32 type), and it runs to the end of the resource. Entry 0 is normally a null key. I sampled 2,025 CASPs (2,000 random zlib/uncompressed ones plus all 25 RefPack ones). In 2,025/2,025 the list ends exactly at end of file. A full header parse, following TS4SimRipper src/CASP.cs for versions 26-52, lands exactly on the list start in 2,000/2,000 Sims 4 CASPs. Version counts: v46 748, v49 386, v42 344, v43 224, v50 157, v51 33.
- The 25 RefPack CASPs are all version 18, which are Sims 3 CASPs (they reference Sims 3 types 0x736884F1, 0x033A1435, 0x062C8204 and 0x0333406C). They sit in sim/16, 19, 21, 29, 31, 33, 40... and are dead weight for Sims 4. None were skipped.
- Header byte-indexes point at the expected types: diffuse to RLE2/LRLE, shadow to RLE2, specular to RLES, normal to _IMG, region map to RMAP, LOD0-3 to GEOM, buff to BUFF, variant thumbnail to _IMG.
- Referenced types in the 2,000: GEOM 11,191, RLE2 3,011, RMAP 1,597, RLES 1,346, _IMG 1,283, LRLE 183, BOND 125, BUFF 27. No THUM keys appear in the lists.
- Exact-key resolution (library / EA game / missing): GEOM 10,455 / 537 / 199; RLE2 2,866 / 75 / 70; RLES 1,296 / 45 / 5; RMAP 1,523 / 71 / 3; _IMG 990 / 0 / 293; LRLE and BOND 100% library.
- Most misses are not real misses. Either the same instance exists under another group (184 GEOM refs in a second 3,000-CASP probe), or the CASP says RLE2 but the library holds that instance as LRLE (94). Refs whose instance exists nowhere: 82 GEOM, 16 RLE2, 10 RLES, 9 _IMG, 7 RMAP.
- THUM (0x3C1AF1F2) really is keyed by the CASP instance. 177,386 of 177,612 library THUM instances (99.87%) equal a CASP instance, and 110,824 of 110,830 in the game. Groups used are 0x2, 0x102, 0x1 and 0x101. Only 28.9% of CC CASP instances ship a thumbnail.
- Object thumbnails OTHM 0x3C2A8647 share the OBJD/COBJ instance (2,301 of 2,388).
- 6,737 library CASP instances override EA part ids. All EA CASP and OBJD ids are below 2^32; CC ids are mostly 64-bit.

(b) Saves and Tray.
- Scanned 44 save files (9 current slots plus 35 backups: .ver and .day.ver) and 1,039 Tray files (107 householdbinary, 181 trayitem, 54 blueprint, 20 room, 677 thumbnail images). That is 8.68 GB uncompressed and 518M values, in 1,058 s with 3 worker processes.
- The walker reads protobuf with no schema, recursing into any blob that parses cleanly, and reads small blobs as packed varint and packed fixed64 lists. The fixed64 case matters: outfit parts are IdList.ids, which is packed fixed64. Blobs that are not protobuf get an unaligned 64-bit scan with numpy.
- I extracted the game's own .proto schemas from Game\Bin\Python\generated.zip and used them to name paths. On Slot_00000018.save I cross-checked against a real schema parse: the generic walk missed 0 values in every category and found extras (for example occult_tracker.occult_sim_infos outfits).
- CAS part ids referenced: 30,280 distinct.
  - 16,520 are EA parts.
  - 7,635 are CC.
  - 593 are CC overrides of EA parts.
  - 5,532 are unknown. 5,528 of these are 64-bit ids found in neither the library nor the game, i.e. CC that is no longer installed; 5,214 of those appear in current slots or Tray.
- Library CASPs worn: 8,228, which is 1.34% of 614,076 (current slots plus Tray only: 7,335). They live in 145 packages (11,916 copies counting duplicates). Top packages: sim/4 561, sim/13 501, sim/m1 444, m2 430, m27 391, m3 380, 128 373.
- A pack of the used CASPs, everything their lists resolve to, and their THUMs is 53,273 unique keys, 7.10 GB on disk (21.5 GB uncompressed). By type: GEOM 4.10 GB, RLE2 1.20 GB, LRLE 1.03 GB, _IMG 0.56 GB, RLES 0.12 GB, THUM 77 MB, CASP 3.3 MB. Current slots only: 6.74 GB. Library total is 259 GB.
- Skin tones (TONE): 40 CC plus 21 overrides used, of 456 CC tones.
- Sculpts (0x9D1AB874): 71 of 177. Face and body sliders (SMOD): 149 and 132 of 503. With their BGEO/DMAP/BOND references that is 918 keys, 49.9 MB.
- Build/buy: 44,495 distinct object definition ids on lots, in inventories and in blueprints. 44,204 are EA, 7 are CC, 9 are CC overrides and 275 are unknown. The 16 used CC objects plus everything their OBJD, MODL and MLOD reference is 74 keys, 343 KB.
- Walls and floors: no CC ids at or above 2^32 were found anywhere in the architecture blobs. That format was not decoded, so this is lower confidence.
- CAS presets (CPRE) cannot be measured: saves store the resulting sculpt and slider values, not which preset was used.
- 223 more CC CASP ids appear only outside outfits: household reward inventory, thrift-store inventory and custom_colors.
